tools.name: wp_site_info
tools.description: Get WordPress site information including name, URL, version, theme, active plugins, content counts, and RTL/text direction detection

tools.name: wp_introspect
tools.description: Get a machine-readable description of this plugin (auth, endpoints, tools, capabilities) so AI clients can self-configure instead of guessing. Compact tool list by default (name + one-line description, no schema). Pass tool="wp_x" to get that one tool's full inputSchema, or full=true to dump every tool's schema (200KB+).

tool.description: Return only this tool's full entry (description, inputSchema, annotations, route) instead of the compact list. Takes precedence over full.

full.description: Return every tool with its full input schema (200KB+) instead of the compact name+description list.

tools.name: wp_onboard
tools.description: Get a complete first-connection briefing for this WordPress site. Returns site identity, content inventory, active integrations, available tools grouped by category, site context, recommended first actions, and a quick reference card. Call this first when connecting to a new site.

sections.description: Allowlist of top-level sections to return: site_identity, content_inventory, active_integrations, available_tools, site_context, recommended_actions, quick_reference, suggested_first_tools, quick_start, pro_active. Omit for the full briefing — available_tools alone is ~95% of that payload; ask for the sections you actually need.

tools.name: wp_list_design_references
tools.description: List stored design references that models can reuse when building pages, archetypes, and Elementor parts from uploaded screenshots or approved design images.

page_intent.description: Optional page intent such as landing_page, blog_post, product_page, or service_page.

source_type.description: Optional source type filter such as upload, url, figma, or stitch.

tools.name: wp_get_design_reference
tools.description: Get one stored design reference, including its image, intent, style, reuse notes, and linked archetypes or parts.

tools.name: wp_upload_design_reference
tools.description: Create a reusable design reference from an image (external URL, Base64, or existing media library attachment). Use when a human shares a screenshot or design that should guide future page creation. Retry strategy: if image_url or image_base64 fails, upload the image first with wp_upload_media_from_url or wp_upload_media_b64, then retry with the returned media_id — the media_id path never fails due to image transfer errors.

media_id.description: Existing media library attachment ID. Use this as the fallback if image_url or image_base64 upload fails — upload the image separately first, then pass the resulting ID here.

image_url.description: External image URL to import. If this fails, upload via wp_upload_media_from_url and use media_id instead.

image_base64.description: Base64-encoded image data. If this fails, upload via wp_upload_media_b64 and use media_id instead.

filename.description: Filename when using image_base64 or importing from URL.

page_intent.description: Target page type such as landing_page, blog_post, service_page, or product_page.

archetype_class.description: Archetype class the design best maps to.

style.description: Style label, for example editorial, premium, showcase, or minimal.

analysis_summary.description: Short summary of what matters in the design.

must_keep.description: Array of elements that should be preserved.

avoid.description: Array of design choices to avoid when recreating this reference.

section_outline.description: Ordered list of sections inferred from the design.

source_type.description: Optional source type override: upload, url, base64, figma, stitch, manual, or media.

tools.name: wp_update_design_reference
tools.description: Update metadata for a stored design reference. Use this to refine intent, style, notes, section outline, or linked archetypes after review.

must_keep.description: Array of design requirements to preserve.

avoid.description: Array of design constraints to avoid.

linked_archetype_ids.description: Array of related Elementor archetype template IDs.

linked_part_ids.description: Array of related Elementor part template IDs.

tools.name: wp_analytics
tools.description: Get site analytics including post counts, page counts, comment counts, and user counts

days.description: Number of days for analytics period

tools.name: wp_detect_plugins
tools.description: Detect active plugins and available capabilities (Elementor, WooCommerce, SEO plugins, etc.)

tools.name: wp_get_options
tools.description: Get WordPress reading options (front page, posts page, and related settings)

tools.name: wp_update_options
tools.description: Update WordPress reading options (set static homepage, posts page, visibility)

blog_public.description: Search engine visibility (true to allow indexing)

tools.name: wp_get_site_context
tools.description: Get the site context — a master prompt / style guide that defines design rules, header/footer structure, color palette, typography, predefined sections, and page layout guidelines. Always read this first when building or editing pages.

tools.name: wp_set_site_context
tools.description: Set the site context (AI brief). This is a markdown document that tells AI assistants how to build pages for this site: design tokens, header/footer rules, reusable sections, and page structure templates. Included automatically in wp_introspect.

context.description: Markdown text defining site style rules, header/footer structure, predefined sections, color palette, typography, and page layout guidelines

tools.name: wp_remember
tools.description: Store a structured memory entry that persists across AI sessions. Use namespaces: identity (brand voice, colors, client name), constraints (rules the AI must follow), history (completed work, decisions), preferences (layout patterns, widget choices), contacts (client POC info).

namespace.description: Memory namespace: identity, constraints, history, preferences, or contacts.

value.description: Value to store — string, number, array, or object.

ttl_days.description: Optional TTL in days. 0 = no expiry.

tools.name: wp_recall
tools.description: Retrieve stored memory entries. Pass namespace + key for exact lookup, or namespace + query for keyword search. Leave both empty to return everything.

namespace.description: Namespace filter: identity, constraints, history, preferences, contacts.

query.description: Keyword to search across keys and values.

tools.name: wp_forget
tools.description: Delete a stored memory entry by namespace and key. Removes a saved rule, preference, or value from site memory.

namespace.description: Namespace: identity, constraints, history, preferences, or contacts.

tools.name: wp_list_memories
tools.description: List all stored memory entries, optionally filtered by namespace. Returns grouped structure with all values and timestamps.

tools.name: wp_get_signals
tools.description: Get the proactive site signal feed — actionable issues WordPress has detected without you asking. Signal types: stale_content (old posts), broken_elementor (invalid page data), missing_featured_image, draft_accumulation, pending_update (plugin updates), seo_issue. Each signal has severity (high/medium/low), entity reference, detail, and action_hint.

types.description: Comma-separated signal types to filter (e.g. "stale_content,missing_featured_image"). Leave empty for all types.

since.description: ISO 8601 timestamp — return signals detected after this time.

refresh.description: Recompute signals before returning. Adds latency — use sparingly.

tools.name: wp_list_site_blueprints
tools.description: List all available site blueprints — pre-built multi-page site structures for different business types (law firm, restaurant, SaaS, real estate, portfolio) plus any custom blueprints you've saved. Each blueprint defines pages, sections, menus, and site context ready to deploy.

category.description: Filter by category: professional, hospitality, tech, creative, custom.

tools.name: wp_get_site_blueprint
tools.description: Get a single site blueprint by ID, including full page definitions, section types, menus, and site context.

id.description: Blueprint ID (e.g. "law-firm", "restaurant", "saas", "real-estate", "portfolio", or a custom ID).

tools.name: wp_create_site_blueprint
tools.description: Save a new site blueprint — a reusable multi-page site structure. Blueprints can be deployed to any site to create all pages, menus, and site context in one step.

pages.description: Array of page definitions. Each: {slug, title, template?, sections: []}.

menus.description: Array of menu definitions. Each: {name, items: [slug1, slug2]}.

site_context.description: Site context / AI brief to set when deploying.

category.description: Category for filtering: professional, hospitality, tech, creative, custom.

tools.name: wp_deploy_site_blueprint
tools.description: Deploy a site blueprint: creates all defined pages, navigation menus, and sets site context in one operation. Pages are created as drafts by default. After deployment, use wp_get_blueprint + wp_add_section to build Elementor layouts for each page's section types.

post_status.description: Page status after creation: draft (default) or publish.

name_prefix.description: Optional prefix for page titles (e.g. client name).

tools.name: wp_extract_site_blueprint
tools.description: Analyze the current site and generate a blueprint definition from it. Extracts page structure, Elementor section types, navigation menus, and site context. Use save=true to store the result as a reusable custom blueprint.

save.description: Save the extracted blueprint as a custom blueprint (default false).

tools.name: wp_get_content_graph
tools.description: Get a weighted internal content graph for SEO and internal linking. Returns content nodes, link/taxonomy edges, inbound/outbound counts, hub/rank/freshness signals, menu depth, orphan candidates, headings, and anchor text.

post_types.description: Comma-separated post types to include. Defaults to page,post.

limit.description: Maximum number of content nodes, 1-500. Defaults to 100.

include_drafts.description: Include draft/private content nodes. Defaults to false.

tools.name: wp_suggest_internal_links
tools.description: Suggest internal links for a source post or page using the content graph. Returns existing site URLs only and approval-ready diffs without mutating content.

source_id.description: Source post or page ID that needs internal links.

post_types.description: Comma-separated post types to include. Defaults to page,post.

limit.description: Maximum graph nodes to inspect, 1-500. Defaults to 100.

max_suggestions.description: Maximum suggestions to return, 1-20. Defaults to 5.

include_drafts.description: Include draft/private candidates. Defaults to false.

tools.name: wp_apply_internal_link
tools.description: Apply an accepted internal link suggestion using an existing graph target. Creates an approval request by DEFAULT and appends a native Gutenberg Related paragraph. Bypassing approval (approval_required=false) requires an admin-scoped API key — write/read keys are silently routed through approval.

source_id.description: Source post or page ID to update.

target_id.description: Existing published target post or page ID from the content graph.

anchor.description: Optional link anchor text. Defaults to target title.

approval_required.description: Defaults to true (an approval request is created). Set false only for admin-scoped keys needing an immediate save; write/read keys sending false are silently gated.

approval_note.description: Optional human review note for the pending link insertion.

tools.name: wp_validate_internal_links
tools.description: Validate existing internal links without mutating content. Detects self-links, duplicate targets, weak anchors, missing targets, unpublished targets, and non-canonical URLs.

post_types.description: Comma-separated post types to include. Defaults to page,post.

limit.description: Maximum graph nodes to inspect, 1-500. Defaults to 100.

include_drafts.description: Include draft/private source content. Defaults to false.

tools.name: wp_validate_seo_readiness
tools.description: Validate SEO pre-publish readiness for a post or page without mutating content. Checks title, slug, H1, heading order, meta description, image alt text, internal links, indexability, canonical, robots, sitemap, and schema hints.

id.description: Post or page ID to validate.

tools.name: wp_validate_structured_data
tools.description: Validate structured data for a post or page without mutating content. Inventories JSON-LD, microdata, and schema.org hints, reports parse/shape issues, and recommends schema types that match visible WordPress content.

id.description: Post or page ID to validate.

tools.name: wp_audit_media_seo
tools.description: Audit media SEO for a post or page without mutating content. Checks featured image coverage, content image alt text, filenames, dimensions, file size, lazy-loading hints, and duplicate image use.

id.description: Post or page ID to audit.

tools.name: wp_seo_audit_site
tools.description: Run a read-only SEO site audit summary across recent posts and pages. Aggregates SEO readiness, structured data, media SEO, and content quality issues into prioritized URL-level recommendations.

post_types.description: Comma-separated post types to include. Defaults to page,post.

limit.description: Maximum URLs to audit, 1-50. Defaults to 25.

include_drafts.description: Include draft/private content. Defaults to false.

store.description: Store this run and normalized issues. Defaults to false.

tools.name: wp_get_seo_issues
tools.description: List stored SEO issue records from stored audit runs. Filter by status, severity, category, post ID, or run ID.

category.description: Category such as readiness, structured_data, media, or content_quality.

post_id.description: Filter issues for a post/page ID.

run_id.description: Filter issues first or last seen in a stored audit run.

limit.description: Maximum issues to return, 1-200. Defaults to 50.

tools.name: wp_run_seo_autofix_plan
tools.description: Build an approval-safe SEO autofix plan from stored SEO issues. This is read-only: it tells agents which fixes can be prepared, which tool/playbook to use, and why every publish-facing change still needs approval.

severity.description: Filter by severity: error, warning, or info.

category.description: Filter by issue category such as readiness, structured_data, media, or content_quality.

post_id.description: Filter issues for a post/page ID.

run_id.description: Filter issues first or last seen in a stored audit run.

issue_id.description: Plan a single stored issue by ID.

limit.description: Maximum issues to inspect, 1-200. Defaults to 50.

tools.name: wp_import_search_performance
tools.description: Import provider-neutral search performance rows from Google Search Console, Bing Webmaster Tools, rank trackers, or a manual export. Stores evidence only; does not fetch external APIs or mutate SEO content.

provider.description: Provider slug: google_search_console, bing_webmaster, or manual.

source.description: Optional source label such as export filename, date range, or connector name.

rows.description: Rows with date, url or page, query, clicks, impressions, ctr, and position.

url.description: Page URL. Either url or page is required.

page.description: Alternate key for the page URL, used if url is absent.

ctr.description: Click-through rate (0-1). Derived from clicks/impressions if omitted.

tools.name: wp_get_seo_trends
tools.description: Read stored search performance trends from imported Search Console/Bing/manual rows. Returns summary, top queries, top URLs, daily aggregates, and import history as read-only SEO evidence.

days.description: Lookback window in days, 1-365. Defaults to 90.

limit.description: Maximum grouped rows to return, 1-100. Defaults to 20.

tools.name: wp_get_woocommerce_seo_report
tools.description: Get a read-only WooCommerce SEO intelligence report for products. Inspects product content depth, short descriptions, category evidence, images, price/schema signals, stock review opportunities, and imported search performance evidence.

status.description: Product status: publish, draft, private, or any. Defaults to publish.

limit.description: Maximum products to inspect, 1-100. Defaults to 25.

tools.name: wp_audit_content_quality
tools.description: Audit content quality and AI-search citation readiness for a post or page without mutating content. Checks answer depth, summaries, FAQ/question coverage, entity-like names, freshness, trust signals, and reference hints.

id.description: Post or page ID to audit.

tools.name: wp_keyword_research
tools.description: Discover related searches, long-tail keywords, and question clusters for any seed phrase using Google Suggest autocomplete. Keyless and free by default — no API key required, no cost, safe to call repeatedly in an autonomous content-marketing loop. Returns a deduplicated keyword set and grouped questions to fuel SEO topic expansion, content ideas, and blog post planning. Similar to AnswerThePublic. Pass enrich=true to also attach DataForSEO market metrics (search volume, CPC, competition, keyword difficulty) when DataForSEO is configured — that spends DataForSEO credit, so call it explicitly per topic you actually intend to act on, not from inside a loop over every candidate.

seed.description: Seed keyword phrase to expand, e.g. "organic coffee".

hl.description: Language code for Google Suggest, and (when enrich=true) the DataForSEO language_code (default: en).

gl.description: Country code for Google Suggest (default: us). When enrich=true, only "us" currently maps to a DataForSEO location — any other value returns enrichment_reason "locale_not_supported" rather than mismatched market data.

max.description: Overall cap on returned suggestion items, 1-500. Defaults to 100.

enrich.description: When true and DataForSEO is configured, attach market metrics (search volume, CPC, competition, keyword difficulty) to each result. Spends DataForSEO credit — call explicitly per topic, not in a loop. Defaults to false (keyless, free, autocomplete-only).

tools.name: wp_get_custom_css
tools.description: Get the Additional CSS from the WordPress Customizer. Returns the full CSS string currently applied to the site.

tools.name: wp_set_custom_css
tools.description: Set or append CSS to the WordPress Customizer Additional CSS. Use mode "append" to add new rules without removing existing ones, or "replace" to overwrite all custom CSS. CSS is applied site-wide immediately.

css.description: CSS code to set or append

mode.description: How to apply: "replace" overwrites all CSS, "append" adds to existing (default)

tools.name: wp_delete_custom_css
tools.description: Delete all Additional CSS from the WordPress Customizer. Removes all custom CSS rules. Returns the previous CSS length.

tools.name: wp_get_css_length
tools.description: Get the length and line count of the Additional CSS without returning the full CSS body. Lightweight check to see if custom CSS exists.

tools.name: wp_get_rendered_html
tools.description: Fetch the rendered HTML of a page as the browser sees it. Useful for verifying CSS, fonts, meta tags, and actual content rendering. Supports CSS selector extraction (tag, .class, #id). Only same-host URLs allowed (SSRF-safe).

id.description: Post or page ID to fetch rendered HTML for

url.description: URL to fetch (same-host only). Either id or url is required.

max_bytes.description: Maximum response size in bytes (default 51200, max 204800)

tools.name: wp_get_rendered_copy
tools.description: Return the structured visible text of a live page — headings, paragraphs, button labels, list items, link text, and image alt text — extracted from the rendered HTML, not from post_content. This is the ground-truth answer to "what does the live page actually say?" and reflects Elementor, Gutenberg, and SEO plugin output. Use before auditing copy, validating content, or comparing what is stored vs what visitors see.

id.description: Post or page ID. Either id or url is required.

url.description: URL to fetch (same-host only). Either id or url is required.

include_chrome.description: Include nav/header/footer text (default false — body content only)

tools.name: wp_list_menus
tools.description: List all navigation menus (including unassigned ones) with id, name, slug, and item count

tools.name: wp_list_menu_locations
tools.description: List all theme menu locations with assigned menu names and IDs. Use to find where navigation menus are displayed.

tools.name: wp_setup_menu
tools.description: Create a menu, add page links, and assign it to a theme menu location

page_ids.description: Array of page IDs to add as menu items

overwrite.description: If true, creates a new menu even if name exists

tools.name: wp_list_menu_items
tools.description: List all items in a menu with their titles, URLs, types, and parent/child relationships

menu_id.description: Menu ID to list items for

tools.name: wp_add_menu_item
tools.description: Add a menu item: custom link (any URL), post type (page, post, product), or taxonomy (category, tag). Supports sub-menus via parent_id.

menu_id.description: Menu ID to add item to

type.description: Item type: 'custom' (URL link), 'post_type' (page/post/product), or 'taxonomy' (category/tag)

object.description: Object type for post_type/taxonomy items (e.g., page, product, category)

parent_id.description: Parent menu item ID to create a sub-menu item

classes.description: CSS classes for styling this menu item

description.description: Item description (used as tooltip or subtitle by some themes)

tools.name: wp_update_menu_item
tools.description: Update an existing menu item: rename its title, change URL, move to different parent, or reposition. Get menu_id from wp_list_menus; get item_id from wp_list_menu_items. If menu_id is unknown, use wp_update_menu_item_auto (item_id only).

item_id.description: Menu item ID — get from wp_list_menu_items. If menu_id is unknown, use wp_update_menu_item_auto instead.

parent_id.description: New parent menu item ID (0 for top level)

classes.description: CSS classes for styling this menu item

description.description: Item description (used as tooltip or subtitle by some themes)

tools.name: wp_delete_menu_item
tools.description: Remove a single item from a WordPress navigation menu by item ID. Use to clean up or restructure navigation.

tools.name: wp_reorder_menu_items
tools.description: Reorder and reparent navigation menu items in a single call. Use to restructure menu hierarchy or move items.

parent_id.description: New parent menu item ID (0 for top level).

tools.name: wp_delete_menu
tools.description: Delete an entire navigation menu and all its items. Use when removing or replacing a navigation menu.

tools.name: wp_assign_menu_location
tools.description: Assign a menu to a theme menu location without modifying menu items

location.description: Theme menu location key (e.g., primary, footer)

tools.name: wp_update_page_template
tools.description: Change a page template (e.g., default, elementor_header_footer, elementor_canvas)

tools.name: wp_list_page_templates
tools.description: List all available page templates for the active WordPress theme. Use to find template options before assigning one to a page.

tools.name: wp_bulk_find_replace
tools.description: Search and replace text in Elementor data across the site, a post type, a list of ids, or one post. Replacement is performed on the decoded element tree (not the raw JSON string) to prevent JSON corruption. Safe for URLs and text. Use dry_run first: it reports per-post match counts without writing.

id.description: One post or page ID. Omit to scope by post_type / ids, or to run site-wide.

ids.description: Post IDs to limit the run to.

post_type.description: Limit to one post type (e.g. post, page, or a custom type). Default: every type with Elementor data.

scope.description: Pass "site" to run across every Elementor post (admin-scoped key required, as for post_type). Site-wide is opt-in; an empty ids list is refused, never widened.

allow_compounding.description: Confirm a replacement that contains its own search text ("Acme" → "Acme Group"), which would compound on a retry. Refused otherwise.

offset.description: Resume point (next_offset) from a truncated run. Runs touch at most 200 posts each.

dry_run.description: Report what would change, per post, without writing. Default false.

search.description: Text to search for in Elementor data

tools.name: wp_get_kit_css
tools.description: Read the Elementor Kit global CSS. Returns custom CSS rules applied site-wide via the Elementor Kit settings.

tools.name: wp_set_kit_css
tools.description: Write global CSS to the Elementor kit. Reliable alternative to wp_set_custom_css — bypasses WordPress Customizer output order and child theme cascade issues. Works on any Elementor site without Elementor Pro. Default mode is replace; use append to add without clobbering existing rules. For CSS you plan to update across multiple build passes (e.g. a template library's shared styles), prefer wp_upsert_kit_css_block instead — append duplicates content on every retry.

css.description: CSS to write to the kit global stylesheet

mode.description: replace (default) overwrites existing kit CSS; append adds to it

tools.name: wp_list_kit_css_blocks
tools.description: List named, hash-tagged Kit CSS blocks managed via wp_upsert_kit_css_block. Returns name/hash/byte count for each — not the CSS body itself, use wp_get_kit_css_block for that.

tools.name: wp_get_kit_css_block
tools.description: Get one named Kit CSS block's full CSS body and content hash.

tools.name: wp_upsert_kit_css_block
tools.description: Create or update a named, idempotent region inside the Elementor Kit CSS, without touching any other block or any unmanaged CSS elsewhere in the kit. Re-submitting identical CSS is a no-op (reported as "skipped") instead of growing the kit — use this instead of wp_set_kit_css mode=append when the same CSS may be written more than once across build/polish passes. Pass expected_hash (from a prior wp_get_kit_css_block/wp_list_kit_css_blocks call) to fail with a conflict if the block changed since you last read it.

name.description: Block name — 1-64 lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, or underscores, starting with a letter or digit

expected_hash.description: Optional optimistic-concurrency hash from a prior read

tools.name: wp_delete_kit_css_block
tools.description: Delete a named Kit CSS block. All other CSS in the kit (other blocks and any unmanaged CSS) is left untouched.

tools.name: wp_list_media
tools.description: List media library items with IDs, URLs, titles, alt text, and MIME types. Before uploading an image, search here first — reuse existing media IDs to avoid duplicates. Filter by mime_type "image" to get only images. Use returned IDs with wp_set_elementor, wp_set_featured_image, or wp_upload_design_reference.

search.description: Search media by title or filename

tools.name: wp_list_content
tools.description: List content for any post type (e.g., WooCommerce products) with search and pagination

post_type.description: Post type to list (e.g., product, lp_course)

tools.name: wp_delete_content
tools.description: Delete a single content item by post type and ID (supports CPT like product)

tools.name: wp_search
tools.description: Search posts and pages by query string with pagination and status filters

status.description: Status filter (publish, draft, pending, private, any)

tools.name: wp_fetch
tools.description: Fetch a single post or page by its WordPress ID or public URL. Returns content, status, metadata, and edit URL.

id.description: Post or page ID (use id or url)

tools.name: wp_list_posts
tools.description: List posts with optional filters. Supports custom post types including wp_block (reusable blocks/synced patterns). Use ids to fetch specific posts and fields to control which data is returned (e.g. fields=id,title,word_count to get word counts without full content).

post_type.description: Post type (default: post). Use wp_block for reusable blocks/synced patterns, or any public custom post type.

status.description: Post status filter (publish, draft, pending, private)

fields.description: Comma-separated field names to return (e.g. "id,title,word_count,content"). id is always included. Use "content" or "word_count" to include full content and word counts.

tools.name: wp_create_post
tools.description: Create a new blog post. Defaults to draft — confirm before publishing. Supports custom post types: post_type=wp_block creates a reusable block/synced pattern, post_type=elementor_snippet creates Elementor Custom Code (requires Elementor Pro). To assign categories or tags, use wp_list_categories / wp_list_tags first to get their IDs.

content.description: Post body (HTML or Gutenberg block markup). Omit for Elementor posts — set content via wp_set_elementor after creation.

status.description: Publication status: "draft" (default, no public URL until published), "publish" (immediately live), "pending" (queued for review), "private" (admin-only visible)

post_type.description: Post type. Default "post". Use "wp_block" for reusable blocks/synced patterns, "elementor_snippet" for Elementor Custom Code injection.

excerpt.description: Short summary shown in archives and feeds. Also used as the SEO meta description fallback when no per-post description is set (AIOSEO/Yoast behavior).

slug.description: URL path segment (e.g. "summer-recipes"). WordPress auto-generates from title if omitted. Must be lowercase, hyphens only.

categories.description: Array of category IDs to assign (e.g. [3, 7]). Get IDs from wp_list_categories. Replaces the post's entire category list.

tags.description: Array of tag slugs or names to assign (e.g. ["recipes", "summer"]). Creates tags that don't yet exist. Replaces the post's entire tag list.

elementor_location.description: For elementor_snippet posts only: where the code injects — "head" (default, before </head>), "body_start" (after <body>), "body_end" (before </body>).

terms.description: Custom taxonomy terms to assign, as {taxonomy: [ids, slugs or names]}. Replaces each named taxonomy's current set. Unknown taxonomy or term is refused before any write. Use categories/tags for the built-in ones.

meta.description: Post meta to write, as {key: value}. Registered meta runs through its registered sanitize callback; unregistered strings are reduced to post-safe HTML (URLs keep their %20). Protected/reserved keys (leading underscore, _elementor_*, mcpwp_*) are refused.

tools.name: wp_update_post
tools.description: Update an existing blog post. Only fields you include are changed — omitted fields are untouched. To change categories or tags, pass the full desired list (replaces current). To set the featured image, use wp_set_featured_image instead.

content.description: Post body (HTML). For Elementor posts, use wp_set_elementor / wp_edit_widget instead — post_content is empty on Elementor pages.

excerpt.description: Short summary for archives and feeds. Acts as SEO meta description fallback in most SEO plugins.

slug.description: URL path segment. Changing this breaks existing links unless you have redirect plugins.

categories.description: Array of category IDs. Replaces all current categories. Get IDs from wp_list_categories.

tags.description: Array of tag slugs or names. Replaces all current tags. Creates tags that don't exist.

terms.description: Custom taxonomy terms to assign, as {taxonomy: [ids, slugs or names]}. Replaces each named taxonomy's current set. Unknown taxonomy or term is refused before any write. Use categories/tags for the built-in ones.

meta.description: Post meta to write, as {key: value}. Registered meta runs through its registered sanitize callback; unregistered strings are reduced to post-safe HTML (URLs keep their %20). Protected/reserved keys (leading underscore, _elementor_*, mcpwp_*) are refused.

tools.name: wp_delete_post

tools.name: wp_list_pages
tools.description: List pages with optional filters for status, search, and pagination. Use ids to fetch specific pages and fields to control which data is returned (e.g. fields=id,title,word_count).

status.description: Page status filter (publish, draft, pending, private)

fields.description: Comma-separated field names to return (e.g. "id,title,word_count,content"). id is always included. Use "content" or "word_count" to include full content and word counts.

tools.name: wp_create_page
tools.description: Create a new WordPress page. Defaults to draft — confirm before publishing. For Elementor pages, create first then set layout via wp_set_elementor. To use a full-width Elementor layout, set template to "elementor_header_footer" (no header/footer) or "elementor_canvas" (completely blank).

title.description: Page title (shown in browser tab and admin list)

content.description: Page body (HTML or Gutenberg block markup). Omit for Elementor pages — set layout via wp_set_elementor after creation.

excerpt.description: Page excerpt/deck. Some templates render this as hero subtitle copy (e.g. a page-templates/editorial-home.php deck).

status.description: Publication status: "draft" (default, not publicly visible), "publish" (immediately live), "pending", "private"

slug.description: URL path segment (e.g. "about-us" → yoursite.com/about-us/). Auto-generated from title if omitted.

parent.description: Parent page ID for hierarchical pages (e.g. "Services" is parent of "Web Design"). Creates nested URLs: /services/web-design/. Use 0 or omit for top-level.

template.description: Page template slug. "default" = theme default. "elementor_header_footer" = Elementor full-width (keeps header/footer). "elementor_canvas" = completely blank canvas. Use wp_list_page_templates to see all available templates.

menu_order.description: Sort order among sibling pages (lower = first). Used by some themes and menus. Default 0.

terms.description: Custom taxonomy terms to assign, as {taxonomy: [ids, slugs or names]}. Replaces each named taxonomy's current set. Unknown taxonomy or term is refused before any write. Use categories/tags for the built-in ones.

meta.description: Post meta to write, as {key: value}. Registered meta runs through its registered sanitize callback; unregistered strings are reduced to post-safe HTML (URLs keep their %20). Protected/reserved keys (leading underscore, _elementor_*, mcpwp_*) are refused.

tools.name: wp_update_page
tools.description: Update an existing WordPress page. Only fields you include are changed — omitted fields are untouched. For Elementor layout changes use wp_edit_widget / wp_add_section / wp_set_elementor instead — post_content is empty on Elementor pages.

content.description: Page body (HTML or Gutenberg). For Elementor pages, use wp_set_elementor / wp_edit_widget instead.

excerpt.description: Page excerpt/deck. Some templates render this as hero subtitle copy (e.g. a page-templates/editorial-home.php deck).

slug.description: URL path segment. Changing this breaks existing links unless a redirect plugin is active.

parent.description: Parent page ID for nested hierarchy. Use 0 to move to top level.

template.description: Page template slug. Common values: "default", "elementor_header_footer", "elementor_canvas". Use wp_list_page_templates to see all available templates.

menu_order.description: Sort order among sibling pages. Lower numbers appear first.

terms.description: Custom taxonomy terms to assign, as {taxonomy: [ids, slugs or names]}. Replaces each named taxonomy's current set. Unknown taxonomy or term is refused before any write. Use categories/tags for the built-in ones.

meta.description: Post meta to write, as {key: value}. Registered meta runs through its registered sanitize callback; unregistered strings are reduced to post-safe HTML (URLs keep their %20). Protected/reserved keys (leading underscore, _elementor_*, mcpwp_*) are refused.

tools.name: wp_delete_page
tools.description: Delete a page (moves to trash by default, use force for permanent deletion)

tools.name: wp_clone_page
tools.description: Duplicate a page including its content, Elementor data, template, and featured image

title.description: Title for the cloned page (defaults to original with Copy suffix)

status.description: Status for cloned page (publish, draft, pending, private)

tools.name: wp_get_page_by_slug
tools.description: Fetch a WordPress page by its URL slug (e.g., "about", "contact"). Use when you know the page URL but not the ID.

tools.name: wp_set_featured_image
tools.description: Set or remove the featured image (thumbnail) for a post or page

media_id.description: Media attachment ID. Use 0 to remove featured image.

tools.name: wp_list_categories
tools.description: List post categories with IDs, names, slugs, and post counts

parent.description: Parent category ID to list children

tools.name: wp_list_tags
tools.description: List all post tags with IDs, names, slugs, and post counts. Use to find tag IDs before assigning them to posts.

tools.name: wp_batch_update
tools.description: Execute multiple REST API operations in a single request (max 100; wp_batch is the same call under the name bulk clients look for). Operations run sequentially and each returns {index, status, data}. Example: [{"method":"PUT","path":"/posts/42","body":{"title":"New Title"}}, {"method":"GET","path":"/pages"}]. Use this to reduce round-trips when making many changes.

operations.description: Array of operation objects. Each must have: method (GET/POST/PUT/DELETE), path (relative to /mcpwp/v1/, e.g. "/pages/42"), body (optional object — used as request body for POST/PUT, query params for GET/DELETE)

body.description: Request body for POST/PUT, or query params for GET/DELETE.

tools.name: wp_batch
tools.description: Run up to 100 REST operations in one round trip. Operations run in order and each returns {index, status, data}; the response adds total, succeeded, failed and spend_budget. A failed operation does not stop the rest, and nothing is rolled back. Costs one rate-limit slot per operation. Operations also draw on the request's spend budget (1000 units: most operations cost 1, a bulk route the items it processes, an operation that spends a site credential or fetches a URL — AI generation, stock photos, screenshots, URL imports — 25 each); once an operation does not fit it and every later one are refused with spend_budget_exhausted and do not run — resend those in a new request. An operation may not target /batch or /mcp. With params._meta.request_id, a batch with any failed operation is not pinned: retry only the failed operations, each under its own request_id. Example: [{"method":"PUT","path":"/posts/42","body":{"title":"New title"}},{"method":"GET","path":"/pages"}].

operations.description: Operations, in order. Each: method (GET/POST/PUT/DELETE), path relative to /mcpwp/v1/ (e.g. "/pages/42"), body (optional object — the request body for POST/PUT, query parameters for GET/DELETE).

body.description: Request body for POST/PUT, or query params for GET/DELETE.

tools.name: wp_upload_media
tools.description: Upload a media file (image, video, etc.) to the WordPress media library

file.description: Base64-encoded file content or file URL

tools.name: wp_upload_media_from_url
tools.description: Upload a single media file from a URL into the WordPress media library. For bulk migrations (5+ images), use wp_bulk_upload_media instead — it avoids hitting the burst rate limit.

url.description: Publicly accessible URL of the file to download and import

filename.description: Override the saved filename on disk (e.g., "ontario-workforce-guide.pdf"). Useful when the source URL has a meaningless slug.

title.description: Media library title shown in WP Admin

tools.name: wp_bulk_upload_media
tools.description: Import up to 20 media files from URLs in a single request. Use this for content migrations instead of looping wp_upload_media_from_url — it counts as one request against the rate limit, not one per image. Pass "urls" for simple imports or "items" for title/alt metadata per file. Returns uploaded[] and failed[] arrays.

urls.description: Simple list of publicly accessible image/file URLs to import. Use "items" instead if you need per-file title or alt text.

items.description: Structured list for importing with metadata. Each item: {url (required), title, alt, filename}.

tools.name: wp_upload_media_b64
tools.description: Upload a media file from Base64 encoded data. Safer than multipart uploads on shared hosting (bypasses ModSecurity).

data.description: Base64-encoded file content (optionally with data URI prefix)

mime_type.description: MIME type (e.g. image/png, image/svg+xml). Inferred from filename when omitted.

tools.name: wp_delete_media
tools.description: Delete a media attachment from the WordPress media library. Permanently removes the file. Confirm with user first.

force.description: Permanently delete instead of trashing (default: false)

tools.name: wp_update_media
tools.description: Update an existing media attachment — change alt text, title, caption, or description without re-uploading

tools.name: wp_list_drafts
tools.description: List all draft posts and pages. Use to review unpublished content or find work in progress.

type.description: Post type filter (post, page, all)

tools.name: wp_delete_all_drafts
tools.description: Bulk delete all draft posts and pages. Permanent — cannot be undone. Always confirm with user first.

type.description: Post type filter (post, page, all)

tools.name: wp_get_elementor
tools.description: Get the full Elementor JSON data for a page or post. Returns sections, columns, widgets, and settings — or, on a site with Elementor Atomic Elements (Editor V4) active, container/leaf elements (e-div-block, e-heading, ...) with props/styles. Check elementor_layout_mode from wp_onboard before editing — it reports "section", "container", or "atomic".

strip_defaults.description: Strip default widget settings to reduce payload size by 70-80%

include_raw.description: Also include elementor_json (raw JSON string duplicate of elementor_data). Off by default — doubles the payload.

element_id.description: Return only the subtree of this one element (id from wp_get_elementor_summary) instead of the whole page. 404 if not found. Omit for the full page.

tools.name: wp_get_elementor_bulk
tools.description: Get Elementor data for multiple pages in a single request (max 25). Returns results keyed by page ID with any errors listed separately. Useful for site audits and bulk operations.

tools.name: wp_get_elementor_summary
tools.description: ALWAYS call this first before editing Elementor pages. Returns a lightweight structural summary with element IDs (needed for add/remove/replace/edit), section types, widget types, and key settings. Every element includes its ID and top-level sections include their index. Atomic Elements (e-div-block, e-heading, ...) are summarized too, with their props unwrapped for display. Use this instead of wp_get_elementor when you only need to understand the page structure.

tools.name: wp_edit_section
tools.description: Surgically edit a single Elementor element without downloading/uploading the full page JSON. Find the target by element_id, section_index (0-based), or search criteria (find). Merges settings into the element and returns only the modified element. Much more token-efficient than get+set for small edits.

element_id.description: Elementor element ID to edit (from summary or previous get)

find.description: Search criteria to find element: {widgetType: "heading", "settings.title": "Old Text"}

settings.description: Settings to merge into the found element

delete_settings.description: Setting keys to remove from the element

convert.description: Set true to convert a page that has existing non-Elementor content. Without it the write is refused rather than destroying that content (#788).

tools.name: wp_edit_widget
tools.description: Edit a single Elementor widget by ID on a page. Updates widget settings without replacing the full page data. More efficient than get+set for updating text, colors, or other widget properties. Widget must be a widget element, not section or container — or, on Atomic Elements (Editor V4) sites, a leaf content element (e-heading, e-button, e-image, e-svg, e-divider, e-youtube, e-self-hosted-video, e-paragraph). For atomic elements, settings values must be wrapped as {"$$type": "<kind>", "value": <actual>} — call wp_get_widget_schema(widget_type) to see the expected kind per prop.

widget_id.description: Elementor widget element ID, from wp_get_elementor_summary or a previous get

settings.description: Settings to merge into the widget (e.g. {"title": "New Heading", "align": "center"})

delete_settings.description: Setting keys to remove from the widget

tools.name: wp_add_section
tools.description: Add a new section/container to an Elementor page at a specific position. No need to send the full page — just the new section. WORKFLOW: 1) wp_get_elementor_summary → get IDs for positioning 2) Build JSON manually or via wp_get_blueprint 3) wp_add_section(id, element, position) 4) Verify response has meta_verified=true.

element.description: The section/container element object with elType, elements[], and settings

convert.description: Set true to convert a page that has existing non-Elementor content. Without it the write is refused rather than destroying that content (#788).

tools.name: wp_remove_section
tools.description: Remove a section/container from an Elementor page by its element ID. Searches both top-level and nested elements.

element_id.description: The Elementor element ID to remove

tools.name: wp_replace_section
tools.description: Replace an entire section/container in an Elementor page by its element ID. The new element takes the position of the old one. Get the target element ID from wp_get_elementor_summary first.

element_id.description: The Elementor element ID to replace

convert.description: Set true to convert a page that has existing non-Elementor content. Without it the write is refused rather than destroying that content (#788).

tools.name: wp_patch_elementor
tools.description: Apply multiple operations to an Elementor page in a single read-write cycle (max 20 ops). More efficient than calling add/remove/replace individually. Operations: add, remove, replace, settings. Get element IDs from wp_get_elementor_summary first. Pass repair_ids=true (operations optional) to rewrite element ids that are not exactly 7 alphanumeric characters — Elementor Pro's Search live results and Taxonomy Filter/Loop Grid AJAX reject them — and repoint the references Elementor resolves (Taxonomy Filter selected_element, Off-canvas links); the response's id_repair lists every old -> new id. Like any validated write, it also applies the validator's standard fixes, reported in warnings.

operations.description: Array of operations (maximum 20). Each: {op: "add"|"remove"|"replace"|"settings", element_id: "...", element: {...}, position: "...", settings: {...}, delete_settings: [...]}. Required unless repair_ids is true.

element_id.description: Target element ID (required for remove, replace, settings)

element.description: New/replacement element object (required for add, replace)

position.description: Insert position for add: start, end, before:{id}, after:{id}

delete_settings.description: Setting keys to remove (for settings op)

repair_ids.description: Rewrite every element id on the page that is not exactly 7 alphanumeric characters to a 7-character id derived from the page and the old id (the same page always gets the same ids), after the operations run, and repoint references Elementor resolves (selected_element, Off-canvas dynamic tags and links). Existing ids are otherwise never rewritten, because CSS (.elementor-element-<id>) and other widgets refer to them; the response's id_repair lists old -> new ids and possible_references to update by hand.

convert.description: Set true to convert a page that has existing non-Elementor content. Without it the write is refused rather than destroying that content (#788).

tools.name: wp_set_elementor
tools.description: FULL PAGE REPLACEMENT — overwrites all Elementor data on the page. For surgical edits, prefer wp_add_section, wp_replace_section, wp_edit_section, or wp_edit_widget instead. Use dry_run=true to validate data without saving. For large payloads with HTML content, use elementor_data_base64 (base64-encoded JSON) instead of elementor_data to avoid quoting/escaping issues. Check elementor_layout_mode from wp_site_info first: sending "container" elements to a "section"-mode site, or Atomic Elements (e-div-block, e-heading, ...) to a site without the Atomic Elements experiment active, is rejected up front with a clear error rather than silently losing data. On an "atomic"-mode site, prefer container + classic widgets — they render correctly; Atomic Elements are accepted and saved but not yet confirmed to render, so check render_verified in the response before trusting an atomic write.

elementor_data.description: Elementor JSON data. For large payloads with HTML, prefer elementor_data_base64 instead.

elementor_data_base64.description: Base64-encoded Elementor JSON data. Use this instead of elementor_data for large payloads containing HTML or special characters to avoid quoting/escaping corruption. Encode your JSON string with btoa() or base64_encode() before sending.

dry_run.description: If true, validate only — no changes are saved. Returns warnings and fixes without writing to database.

repair_ids.description: Rewrite element ids in the data you send that are not exactly 7 alphanumeric characters (Elementor Pro's Search and Taxonomy Filter/Loop Grid AJAX reject them) to 7-character ids derived from the page and the old id, repointing selected_element and Off-canvas references. The response's id_repair lists old -> new ids and settings that may still name an old id. Combine with dry_run=true to preview: the same data on the same page always gets the same ids, so the preview is what the write applies.

convert.description: Set true to convert a page that has existing non-Elementor content. Without it the write is refused rather than destroying that content (#788).

tools.name: wp_elementor_status
tools.description: Check if Elementor is active and get Elementor status information

tools.name: wp_regenerate_elementor_css
tools.description: Regenerate Elementor CSS for a specific page or the entire site. Use after updating Elementor data via API to ensure styles are applied. Returns detailed per-page results: regenerated, skipped (with reason), and failed (with error). Use force=true to delete existing CSS files before regenerating.

id.description: Page ID to regenerate CSS for. Omit to regenerate all site CSS.

force.description: Delete existing CSS files before regenerating (default: false)

tools.name: wp_get_elementor_widgets
tools.description: Get list of available Elementor widgets. Pass a widget type name to get its full controls schema with valid control keys, types, defaults, and options.

widget_type.description: Widget type name (e.g. "heading", "image", "nav-menu") to get full controls schema. Omit to list all widgets.

search.description: List mode only: case-insensitive substring match against widget name, title, and description.

category.description: List mode only: filter to widgets whose reference category matches exactly.

fields.description: List mode only: allowlist of per-widget keys to return (e.g. ["name","category"]). Omit for every field.

tools.name: wp_get_widget_schema
tools.description: Get the detailed controls schema for a specific Elementor widget type. Returns all valid control keys grouped by tab (content, style, advanced) with types, labels, defaults, and options. Use this to discover valid settings keys before building pages.

tab.description: Return controls from only this tab (content, style, or advanced). Omit for every tab.

fields.description: Allowlist of top-level result keys to return (e.g. ["tabs"] or ["description","example","common_mistakes"]). Omit for every field.

tools.name: wp_elementor_widget_help
tools.description: Get complete help for an Elementor widget type: all valid settings keys with types and defaults, example JSON element, and common mistakes to avoid. Works offline (no Elementor installation required). Use this BEFORE building Elementor pages to ensure correct settings keys. If widget_type is not found, returns closest matches.

widget_type.description: Widget type name (e.g. "heading", "image", "button", "icon-box", "price-table"). Use exact Elementor widget type names.

tools.name: wp_preview_elementor
tools.description: Get rendered HTML preview of a page built with Elementor. Useful for reading content or checking layout before edits. Returns HTML output, text summary, and element statistics (sections, columns, widgets, widget types, word count). Use "summary" format (default) to save tokens — returns truncated text + stats without HTML. Use "text" for full text extraction, or "html" for full rendered HTML.

format.description: Output format: "summary" (text truncated to 500 chars + stats, no HTML — default, saves tokens), "text" (full plain text extraction), "html" (full rendered HTML + text)

tools.name: wp_screenshot_url
tools.description: Take a screenshot of a URL. Uses Cloudflare Browser Rendering (headless Chromium) if configured, otherwise falls back to WordPress mshots. By default the screenshot is saved to the media library and returned as a URL (base64 payloads overflow AI-client contexts); pass inline=true for raw base64. Set webhook_url for async mode — the webhook fires when the screenshot is ready.

save_to_media.description: Also save screenshot to WordPress media library

inline.description: Return raw base64 image data instead of a media-library URL. Off by default — base64 (500KB+) overflows AI-client contexts.

webhook_url.description: URL to POST when screenshot is ready. Enables async mode for mshots. Payload: {url, screenshot_url, status, timestamp}. Header: X-SPAI-Event: screenshot.ready

tools.name: wp_list_api_keys
tools.description: List all MCPWP API keys with scopes and metadata. Does not return secret values.

tools.name: wp_create_api_key
tools.description: Create a role-based API key. Roles limit which MCP tool categories the key can access. Returns plaintext key once.

role.description: Access role: admin (all tools), author (content/media/taxonomy), designer (elementor/gutenberg/media/site), editor (content/media/taxonomy/seo), custom (pick categories)

tool_categories.description: Tool categories to allow (only for custom role). Options: content, media, taxonomy, elementor, gutenberg, seo, forms, site, admin, webhooks

scopes.description: Key scopes (read, write, admin). Auto-set for non-admin roles.

allow_destructive.description: Exempt this key from the destructive-operation approval gate. Honoured only when the key is created by an administrator in wp-admin; sent through the API it is ignored and reported under "ignored".

tools.name: wp_revoke_api_key
tools.description: Revoke a scoped API key by ID. Immediately disables the key — any agent using it will get 401 errors.

tools.name: wp_rate_limit_status
tools.description: Get current rate-limit settings and usage for the calling identifier

tools.name: wp_update_rate_limit
tools.description: Update rate-limit settings for this site (admin only). Sets max requests per window for MCP calls.

burst_limit.description: Requests allowed in short burst window

tools.name: wp_reset_rate_limit
tools.description: Reset rate-limit counters for an identifier (admin only)

identifier.description: Identifier to reset (for example key:<id> or IP)

tools.name: wp_get_plugin_settings
tools.description: Get MCPWP plugin settings. Returns: activity logging config, CORS allowed origins, OAuth settings, alert thresholds, GitHub integration status. Secrets are redacted. Use wp_update_plugin_settings to change values.

tools.name: wp_update_plugin_settings
tools.description: Update MCPWP plugin settings. Pass only the keys you want to change. Allowed keys: enable_logging (bool), log_retention_days (1-365), log_store_response_data (bool), allowed_origins (comma-separated URLs), oauth_enabled (bool), oauth_client_id, oauth_client_secret, oauth_token_ttl (60-86400 seconds), alerts_enabled (bool), alerts_window_minutes (1-60), alerts_cooldown_minutes (1-1440), alerts_5xx_threshold (1-10000), alerts_auth_threshold (1-10000), github_token, github_repo (owner/repo).

log_store_response_data.description: Store response data in activity logs

allowed_origins.description: CORS allowed origins (comma-separated URLs, or empty for default)

alerts_5xx_threshold.description: Server errors in window before alert fires (1-10000)

alerts_auth_threshold.description: Auth failures in window before alert fires (1-10000)

tools.name: wp_check_update
tools.description: Check if a newer version of MCPWP is available. Returns current version, latest version, and download URL.

tools.name: wp_trigger_update
tools.description: Download and install the latest version of MCPWP. The plugin will be upgraded in place. Requires administrator privileges.

tools.name: wp_integrations_status
tools.description: List all available integrations and their configuration status. Shows which providers are configured, when they were set up, and their last test result. Providers include: pexels (stock photos), openai/gemini (AI image gen, vision), elevenlabs (TTS), screenshot (Cloudflare Browser Rendering for screenshots), google_indexing, and figma (design context intake).

tools.name: wp_configure_integration
tools.description: Configure a third-party integration. For single-key providers (pexels, openai, gemini, elevenlabs), pass "key". For multi-field providers like "screenshot", "google_indexing", and "figma", pass "config". Example: provider="figma", config={"access_token":"your-token","default_file_key":"abc123"}

provider.description: Provider slug: pexels, openai, gemini, elevenlabs, screenshot, google_indexing, figma

key.description: API key (for single-key providers: pexels, openai, gemini, elevenlabs)

config.description: Configuration object for multi-field providers. For screenshot: {"url": "worker_url", "token": "auth_token"}. For figma: {"access_token": "personal_access_token", "default_file_key": "optional_file_key"}.

tools.name: wp_test_integration
tools.description: Test a configured integration connection. For screenshot, sends a test request to the worker. For figma, validates the API token and optional default file access. For API providers, validates the API key.

tools.name: wp_remove_integration
tools.description: Remove a configured integration. Deletes the stored API key or configuration for the provider.

tools.name: wp_cloudflare_status
tools.description: Check whether Cloudflare is connected for this site (API token + zone ID configured under Integrations) and report the zone name, status, and plan.

tools.name: wp_cloudflare_fix_mcp_access
tools.description: Self-service fix for the most common Cloudflare/MCP problem: Bot Fight Mode or Security Level silently blocking MCP requests to this site. Creates or updates a Cloudflare Configuration Rule that drops Security Level to "essentially_off" for this site's own /wp-json/mcpwp/v1/* path (the confirmed fix), and best-effort adds a WAF skip rule for Super Bot Fight Mode / Managed Rules on the same path. Requires the Cloudflare integration to be configured first.

tools.name: wp_cloudflare_purge_cache
tools.description: Purge Cloudflare cache for specific URLs (e.g. right after editing a page) or the entire zone. Pass urls as an array, or purge_everything=true.

urls.description: URLs to purge (max 30). Omit if purge_everything is true.

purge_everything.description: Purge the entire zone cache instead of specific URLs.

tools.name: wp_cloudflare_get_speed_settings
tools.description: Read this zone's current Cloudflare Speed settings that affect Core Web Vitals: early_hints, http3, rocket_loader, polish (image optimization).

tools.name: wp_cloudflare_update_speed_setting
tools.description: Toggle one Cloudflare Speed setting for this zone. Valid settings: early_hints, http3, rocket_loader (values: "on"/"off"), polish (values: "off"/"lossless"/"lossy"/"webp").

tools.name: wp_list_webhook_events
tools.description: List all available webhook event names and descriptions. Use to discover events before creating a webhook subscription.

tools.name: wp_get_event_schema
tools.description: Get normalized AI-first event schema with WordPress hook names for agents and webhook subscribers

tools.name: wp_list_mcp_events
tools.description: List recent normalized MCPWP events emitted by approvals, SEO audits, and other agent workflows

type.description: Optional event type filter, for example approval.created or seo.audit_completed

tools.name: wp_list_webhooks
tools.description: List registered webhook endpoints with URL, events, and delivery status. Use to audit webhook subscriptions.

tools.name: wp_create_webhook
tools.description: Create a new webhook endpoint subscription. Registers a URL to receive POST notifications on specified events.

tools.name: wp_update_webhook
tools.description: Update an existing webhook: URL, events, secret, or enabled/disabled status.

tools.name: wp_delete_webhook
tools.description: Permanently delete a webhook subscription and stop all future deliveries.

tools.name: wp_test_webhook
tools.description: Send a test delivery payload to a webhook endpoint. Use to verify the receiving server is working.

tools.name: wp_list_webhook_logs
tools.description: List delivery logs for a webhook. Returns timestamps, response codes, and payload details for debugging.

tools.name: wp_submit_feedback
tools.description: Submit feedback, a bug report, or a feature request to the site owner. Optionally creates a GitHub issue if configured.

type.description: Feedback type: bug_report, feature_request, or feedback

tools.name: wp_list_feedback
tools.description: List submitted feedback entries with optional filters for type and status

type.description: Filter by type: bug_report, feature_request, feedback

status.description: Filter by status: open, acknowledged, resolved, closed, all

tools.name: wp_get_post_meta
tools.description: Get post meta for a post or page. Returns a single key or all non-sensitive meta.

url.description: Optional URL to purge. Omit to flush the entire site cache.

tools.name: wp_get_staging_info
tools.description: Detect the hosting provider and list available staging environments for this site. Returns environment IDs, names, types (staging|production), and URLs. Call this first to discover environment IDs before using push tools. No parameters required.

tools.name: wp_push_to_staging
tools.description: Copy the live (production) environment to staging. Safe and non-destructive — overwrites the staging environment only. Requires the staging integration to be configured in MCPWP > Integrations. On hosts with async APIs (Kinsta) the response includes an operation_id to poll with wp_get_staging_status.

source.description: Source environment ID (live/production). Get valid IDs from wp_get_staging_info.

destination.description: Destination environment ID (staging). Get valid IDs from wp_get_staging_info.

include_db.description: Include the database in the copy (default true).

include_files.description: Include uploaded files/media in the copy (default true).

tools.name: wp_push_to_live
tools.description: Request a staging → live push. IMPORTANT: this tool does NOT push immediately. It creates a pending approval request and returns an approval_id. A human operator must approve the request (via wp_approve_request) before it can be applied (via wp_apply_approval). Always provide a reason describing what changed and why. Marked destructive — irreversible without a backup.

source.description: Source environment ID (staging). Get valid IDs from wp_get_staging_info.

destination.description: Destination environment ID (live/production). Get valid IDs from wp_get_staging_info.

include_db.description: Include the database in the push (default true).

include_files.description: Include uploaded files/media in the push (default true).

reason.description: Required: describe what changed on staging and why it is ready for live.

tools.name: wp_get_staging_status
tools.description: Poll the status of an asynchronous staging push operation. Use the operation_id returned by wp_push_to_staging or wp_push_to_live (after approval + apply). Returns status, progress percentage (if available), and a message from the hosting API.

operation_id.description: Operation ID returned by a push endpoint.
